import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Set a clean style for the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a figure and an axes object
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep,
# while incorporating Stress Level using color (hue) and Physical Activity Level using marker size.
# This allows for a multi-dimensional view of how these key lifestyle factors interact with sleep metrics.
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Stress Level',         # Color points based on Stress Level
    size='Physical Activity Level', # Scale point size based on Physical Activity Level
    sizes=(50, 600),            # Define the range of marker sizes
    palette='viridis',          # Use a perceptually uniform colormap
    alpha=0.8,                  # Set transparency to help visualize overlapping points
    edgecolor='w',              # Add a white edge to points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5               # Line width for the point edges
)

# Set the title and labels for the plot
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by Stress and Physical Activity', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 Scale)', fontsize=12)

# Add a grid for better readability
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
